verdict.rationale: OpenClaw is self-hosted, storing memory as plain Markdown files and session history in local SQLite (docs-24/58/85, docs-25/76), which gives users inherent filesystem-level control over retention/deletion, and secrets management explicitly supports 'safe one-way scrubbing' for credentials (docs-14/95). However there is no documented dedicated data-retention policy, bulk-delete/export command, or GDPR-style data lifecycle tooling beyond secret scrubbing. Missing for 10: explicit data retention policy/documentation, a first-class 'delete all my data' command or audit trail, and any independent confirmation that deletion actually removes data end-to-end.
